subject: Production latency & 5xx surge — dedicated pool headroom drain (CobaltBank)
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@cobaltbank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency & 5xx spike — CobaltBank Dedicated pool

Olga —

We’re seeing a sustained latency increase and 5xx spike on our production inference endpoints that map to our dedicated pool (reservation id: RESV-CB-4982). Key metrics from our monitoring:
- P95 inference latency jumped from ~180ms -> 1.2s in the last 25 minutes
- 5xx rate increased from 0.1% -> 4.7%
- Request throughput reporting at ~75% of our reserved QPS (we're still billed for full reservation)

This started around 07:40 PDT. Users are reporting slow checkout experiences in our risk-scoring flow. We’ve tried restarting a handful of replicas per your runbook; errors persist. Attached is a screen grab from our Grafana and a short tail of errors.

Immediate asks:
1) Can Redwood authorize temporary burst capacity or a short-term uplink to avoid user impact?
2) If we need to fail to a smaller-quantized model / fallback routing, we need guidance on customer-visible degradations.
3) We’ll join a bridge — what’s the quickest channel?

This is affecting their conversion path; we need urgent help.

—Sara
Ops Lead, CobaltBank

Attachments: error_snapshot_0719.png

Subject: Re: Production latency & 5xx spike — CobaltBank Dedicated pool

Sara — thanks for the alert.

Quick triage notes (doing this live):
- I can see the headroom dropping on the dedicated pool that hosts CB’s reservation (RESV-CB-4982). There’s an unusual queue depth pattern; backend QPS is below reservation but tokens-per-request and decode time per token have spiked.
- No obvious infra OOMs yet; kernel starved cycles look correlated with a handful of long-running heavy-context requests.

Immediate next steps from our side (ops checklist attached):
- Can you capture the active KV cache hit rate over the last 30m and paste the per-replica queue depths?
- We’ll spin a temporary burst (pending exec approval) and flip a routing rule to shift non-critical endpoints to a cheaper quantized variant to free headroom.
- If approved, we’ll apply a short-lived prefix cache warm for high-frequency keys.

I’m standing up a 30-min bridge now. Joining link: https://redwood.app/bridges/CB-4982-0719 (ops-only).

Olga
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops_request_checklist.md

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: dedicated pool headroom drain — request for short-term authorization & exec readout

Team —

Escalating an active customer-impacting incident for CobaltBank (RESV-CB-4982). Summary:
- Time window: 07:40 PDT — ongoing
- Symptom: P95 latency and 5xx spike; observed throughput at ~75% of reserved QPS while queueing and decode time per token increased sharply.
- Immediate customer impact: checkout latency & failed risk-score calls, visible to user flow and revenue.

Triage so far (ops):
- Likely contributors: sudden increase in long-context inference requests (higher token lengths), KV cache miss storm, and an unanticipated batching pattern causing head-of-line blocking.
- Short-term mitigations proposed:
  1) Authorize a temporary burst of up to 200% of allocated pool for 2 hours to reduce tail latency while we mitigate.
  2) Apply routing fallback: move low-risk, high-volume endpoints to the quantized/higher-latency model variant (estimated 30% fewer tokens/sec but 40% lower memory footprint).
  3) Warm KV cache and apply prefix caching for the top 50 keys observed in the last 2 weeks.

Customer asks for an explicit timeline and confirmation to proceed; they’re on a bridge and can push a toggle if we sign off. I’ve attached a 1-slide exec readout that summarizes the observed delta (throughput vs reservation) and the expected short-term impact of a burst.

Immediate asks for leadership:
- Vivek: approve emergency burst authorization and short credit/overage guardrail for CobaltBank while we remediate.
- David/Marissa: if approved, please prioritize the routing change and assign one engineer to own the cache-warming job and rollback plan.

I’ve prepared a short customer-facing note below; if you approve the burst I’ll send it as ACK and start the capacity change.

Customer-facing ACK (suggested):
"We acknowledge the service degradation you're seeing and have authorized temporary additional capacity while our engineering team applies targeted mitigations. We expect improved tail latency within 10–20 minutes after capacity is applied and cache warming completes. We will follow up with a detailed post-mortem within 48 hours."

Olga
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: exec_readout_slides.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: dedicated pool headroom drain — request for short-term authorization & exec readout

Approve temporary burst: up to 200% for 2 hours for CobaltBank (RESV-CB-4982).

Please include a one-line credit guardrail limit (max overage $4,000) and log the change in the incident ticket. Marissa/David — prioritize the routing fallback and cache warming immediately; mark the change for automatic rollback at the 2-hour mark unless we confirm stability.

Olga — send the ACK to the customer with the suggested language and include the bridge link. Post-mortem due within 48h.

—Vivek
CTO, Redwood Inference
